messages:
Alex: Quick heads-up — ran a short microbench on the continuous-batcher after the kernel-selector tweak and hit a ~10-14% p95 regression on boxes with high KV cache occupancy. Repro steps below.
Alex: Repro: mixed short+long requests, bursty arrivals (1–3s), kernel selector flag enable_prefetch=true. Observed repeated small evictions and fallback to slower kernels.
Alex: Repro command (local harness):
```bash
./tools/loadtest --profile continuous --burst 50 --model redwood-7b --kernel-selector prefetch
```
Maya: Oof. Any heap/alloc traces or eviction counters? sounds like admission isn't accounting for per-request KV footprint.
Alex: Log snippet: 
```
evict: shard0 bytes=12MB->3MB reason=kv_overflow
kernel: route=fallback_fp32 p95:+32%
```
Tom: We have token_budget today but it's very naive (tokens * avg_kv_per_token). We probably need an empirical KV-footprint estimator that includes prompt length, prefix hits, and kv-entry size distribution.
Lina: Proposal: at queueing time compute kv_est = clamp(estimate_k(req), 1KB, kv_budget_cap). Admit only if headroom > kv_est + reserve_margin (reserve_margin default 8MB). That prevents small bursts from tripping soft-evictions.
Samir: Another lever: transient admission mode — allow a request to enter but mark the batch as "unguarded" and stop admitting new unguarded requests for X ms to let the KV settle. Good for low-latency critical requests.
Maya: We should add perf telemetry: counters for kv_est_per_request, headroom_at_admit, evictions_after_admit, and a histogram for eviction_bytes. Then we can correlate admission events -> evictions -> kernel fallbacks.
Priya: I can run a canary with two knobs: (1) pre-admit kv check enabled, (2) post-admit backoff window of 50ms. Will measure p95, p99, and error rate. ETA EOD.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: created canary redwood/continuous-batcher@canary-kv-safety-2026-03-18 (10% traffic to 3 nodes)
Alex: If canary looks good, follow-ups: (a) adjust kernel route thresholds to prefer quantized kernels under sustained high-KV pressure, (b) add automatic fallback policy that prefers dropping low-priority requests before forcing kernel fallback. File RFC or quick PR?
Tom: I'll draft a short RFC (batching+kv-admission) with perf dashboards and SLA impact analysis. Also will add CI unit that simulates KV churn so we don't regress again.
Maya: SG, tag me on the RFC. Also please add a deterministic repro harness that reproduces the eviction sequence (so we can iterate faster). :thinking_face:
Lina: Action items:
- Priya: run canary + upload perf dump (p95/p99/evictions) by EOD (owner)
- Tom: draft RFC + CI test (owner)
- Alex: add telemetry counters + quick PR for kv_est clamp (owner)
- Samir: sketch transient admission API (owner)
- Maya: review RFC + tests

Alex: Thanks — this should keep the kernel-selection changes from regressing tail latency while we tune admission heuristics.
